title: What is creditable drug coverage?
summary: Medicare Made Clear article explaining creditable drug coverage, how it lets you avoid the Part D late enrollment penalty, how the penalty is calculated, and how to get Part D coverage.

assets.alt: What to know about Medicare Part D when still working

atoms.title: Definition of creditable drug coverage
atoms.question: What is creditable drug coverage?
atoms.text: Medicare defines creditable coverage as coverage that is at least as good as what Medicare provides. Therefore, creditable drug coverage is drug coverage that is as good as or better than Medicare Part D.

atoms.title: Why creditable coverage matters
atoms.question: Why does creditable drug coverage matter?
atoms.text: Creditable drug coverage matters because it may allow you to delay enrolling in Medicare and avoid the Part D late enrollment penalty. The penalty is charged if you enroll in a Medicare Part D plan after your Initial Enrollment Period (IEP) ends and don't qualify for an exception.

When is the Part D late penalty charged?

atoms.title: Steps to delay Part D without penalty
atoms.question: What do I need to do to delay Part D enrollment without a penalty?
atoms.text: To delay Part D enrollment without penalty: 1) make sure you can qualify for a Medicare Special Enrollment Period; 2) get a written notification of creditable coverage from your previous plan; and 3) enroll in a Part D plan within 63 days of losing or leaving your former plan and/or the former creditable drug coverage.

atoms.title: Ask your benefits administrator if still working
atoms.question: How do I find out if my employer plan has creditable drug coverage?
atoms.text: Delaying Part D while keeping other drug coverage is typically seen most for people who plan to keep working past 65. If you are working past age 65 and plan to delay Medicare enrollment, talk with your employee benefits administrator, who can tell you if your employer plan provides creditable drug coverage.

atoms.title: Part D late penalty is 1% per month
atoms.question: How much is the Medicare Part D late enrollment penalty?
atoms.text: The late penalty for Medicare Part D is an additional 1 percent of the premium amount for each month you're late, and you pay the penalty for as long as you have Part D. For example, if you enroll in a Part D plan that starts on November 1 but your IEP ended on June 30, you are four months late and your penalty would be 4 percent of the premium.

atoms.title: How to get Part D coverage
atoms.question: How do I get Medicare prescription drug coverage?
atoms.text: You can get Medicare prescription drug coverage in a stand-alone Part D plan or as part of a Medicare Advantage plan (Part C). Private insurance companies offer the plans under contract with Medicare. You will need to have Part A and/or Part B to get a stand-alone Part D plan, and you will need both Parts A and B to get a Medicare Advantage plan.
